what: MASONRY LANGUAGE PACK (build L1, 2026-10-21): the words for the parts of a brick (and of other masonry units) and how they are recognised. Data for engine/tools/language.py; over engine/packs/generic/language.json.

vocabulary.bed: the face a brick is laid on (upper and lower bed faces); a frog is pressed into a bed face
vocabulary.stretcher: the long side face, shown along the wall's face when the brick is laid lengthwise
vocabulary.header: the short end face, shown when the brick is laid across the wall
vocabulary.frog: the recess in a bed face (floor and walls), to save clay and key the mortar
vocabulary.arris: an edge where two faces meet

sources.what: standard metric brick work size 215 x 102.5 x 65 mm; terms bed, stretcher, header, frog, arris
sources.where: BS EN 771-1 (clay masonry units) / BS 3921:1985; the terms as used in UK bricklaying (e.g. Brick Development Association, 'Brickwork: guidance', glossary)
sources.status: the standard and the terms: well established (estimated reference; not opened in this build)

segmentation.why: a brick is faceted: its parts are its faces and the strips between them

frame: the brick lies on its bed: up (+z) = the upper bed's normal, length along x, width along y (the model's own axes; ingest turns them)

findings._: measured findings (build L1, 2026-10-21): what was done, what resulted, where; evidence, not rules

items.what: A brick segments into its faces, the strips between them and the patches where three meet
items.result: Standard metric brick (215 x 102.5 x 65 mm, a 145 x 55 x 10 mm frog, 2 mm arrises; marching cubes at 1 mm): 11 facets (2 beds, 2 stretchers, 2 headers, frog floor, 4 frog walls), 20 edges (12 arrises, 8 frog edges), 16 corners (8 brick, 8 frog): 47 parts, every face in one, all named by masonry words, 100 % of vertices addressed. A facet = the flat face + the fillet band within 20 deg: stretcher 131.46 cm2 against (211 + 2 x 0.68) x (61 + 2 x 0.68) mm = 132.4 cm2.

items.what: Mirror faces read alike only off the meshing lattice
items.result: With the marching-cubes lattice on the brick's planes, exact zeros there made the stretchers 128.7 and 134.4 cm2 and the frog walls 8.9 and 11.3 cm2; offset by 0.37 voxel both pairs were equal to 0.01 cm2.

items.what: A planar face is addressed in its own plane from its area centroid
items.result: The upper bed is a ring round the frog: an origin at the nearest surface point to its centroid hopped between the two inner edges on a remesh (56 mm). From the area centroid with a ray address (h+), re-voxelised 1.0 -> 0.7 mm: no address of the 47 parts moved more than 0.27 mm (worst part p99); 81 of 3,464 fell just off their part's edge.

items.what: A broken corner leaves the rest of the brick's language in place
items.result: A 20 mm sphere off one corner: that corner reported gone; 43 of the other 46 parts' addresses moved under 0.05 mm (p99), one address over 1 mm (on the header where the material went), 43 of 3,440 miss (in the chip).
